analyst_view.overall: Sporting (10th, 9 points) host Manchester United (17th, 6 points); a win would put Sporting near the top eight, while United need points to stay in the play-off spots. Both have new coaches: Paulo Fonseca at Sporting, who said United are hard to read and expects his side to sit in a low block at times, and Mauricio Pochettino at United, whose first game was a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool. United are without Matheus Cunha (one-match UEFA ban for his red card against Roma), whom the numbers don't list, plus Sesko, Baleba, Ugarte and Rashford (counted); Shaw is a doubt and Zirkzee is expected to lead the line. Fonseca confirmed Ioannidis and Flavio Goncalves are fit, while Debast and Nuno Santos need a few more days (counted). Polish referee Szymon Marciniak (3.5 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already take Sesko off United and now list Rashford too. Cunha's ban is the one thing they don't see, and he is one of United's main attackers, so I take about 4% off, to about 2.8; Ioannidis being fit for Sporting removes the other reason I had for a bigger cut this morning.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, with United slightly more of them. Fonseca expects Sporting to defend deep at times, which could hand United more corners, but Sporting attack wide through Catamo and Araujo at home, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, already lowered about 9% for referee Marciniak's low card count and 11% for Sporting's quiet recent record, and raised 4% for United's busy one. Cunha's ban removes one hot-headed player and Bruno Fernandes' return to his old club adds a little edge, but both are small, so I stay at 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, with United's recent shot volume adding about 9% to their side. Without Cunha, one of their busiest shooters, United's attack rests on Mbeumo, Fernandes and Zirkzee, and Sporting may sit deeper at times, so I trim a little, to about 27.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, split evenly. Cunha's ban, which the numbers don't see, takes one of United's main finishers away, while Sporting have Suarez and Ioannidis fit, so I trim only slightly, to about 10.1.
